name: Sorelianism
summary: Sorelianism is the revolutionary-syndicalist outlook of Georges Sorel. It holds that the working class must keep up an uncompromising class war, using proletarian violence and the myth of the general strike to destroy the bourgeois state and parliamentary politics, instead of seeking social peace or reform. It stresses inspiring myths over scientific forecasts and an ethic of the producers.
scope: The mature Sorel of Reflections on Violence (1908) and the revolutionary-syndicalist doctrine he sets out there. It leaves out his later nationalist and fascist appropriations, his earlier conservative phase and his wartime turn to Lenin; Reflections is the main text and no other Sorel work was read.

missingStatements.text: A revolutionary vision’s value does not depend on whether it comes true.
missingStatements.rationale: Sorel’s letter to Halévy distinguishes myths from forecasts, warning against comparing realised facts with the pre-action picture; chapter IV says the general-strike vision’s factual reality does not determine its value. Galletta explains this myth/utopia distinction as central. The general word vision replaces Sorel’s technical myth to avoid the everyday meaning of a deliberate falsehood, without importing a claim that political lying is acceptable.
